title: feat(spec)!: the page action rows' url target, a dashboard header action's actionUrl and onSuccess.navigate apply the shared url-target refusal
body:
Fixes #23077

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The rest of ruling A+'s url-target family. Ruling A+ on objectstack-ai/objectui#12191 says the scheme set "is stated once in the contract and the runtime fulfils exactly that". PR #23076 (`9b37edbd7`) stated it once, as `navigationTargetRefusal` in `packages/spec/src/ui/navigation-target.ts`, and applied it at the two url-action doors. This PR applies the same function, with no second URL grammar, at the three doors the triage direction (comment 6129646171) names. A target that opens with `${` keeps the predicate's own rule: it is left alone at the door and judged by the runner after interpolation.

## What changed

1. **Page action rows** (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`). One refinement factory, `refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget`, is applied to `ActionButtonPropsSchema` and `ActionIconPropsSchema` (when `actionType: 'url'`) and to the `action:group` and `action:menu` members (when `type: 'url'`). It judges `target` and refuses at `target`. On every other executor `target` names a script, flow, page, endpoint or form, so it is not judged, and a row with no `target` is not judged either. `os validate`'s props gate (`@objectstack/lint` `validateComponentProps`) parses `properties` against these same `ComponentPropsMap` rows, so it now reports the refusal at the row's `target` path, with the parse's own first sentence. The refusal is a `component-props-invalid` finding, a warning, because warning is that gate's only tier (see its module header). The card puts the gate's upgrade to error out of scope. The lint package changes no code; one test file pins the gate's reading.
2. **Dashboard header actions** (`packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`). `DashboardHeaderActionSchema` judges `actionUrl` when `actionType` is `'url'` **or omitted**, and refuses at `actionUrl`. On `flow` / `script` / `modal` / `api` / `form`, `actionUrl` is untouched. The refusal's subject names both spellings of the url route ("a url target when `actionType` is `'url'` or omitted"), so an author who meant a flow learns that declaring `actionType` is the way out.
3. **Post-success navigation** (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`). The `onSuccess` block judges `navigate` on every value and refuses at `onSuccess.navigate`. `${result.redirectUrl}` stays accepted and `/apps/crm/tasks/${result.id}` stays accepted. `tasks/${result.id}` is refused, because the runner refuses `tasks/42` after interpolation too.

The `describe` text and TSDoc on each key now state the set. Three D3 entries are added, one per door: `ui-page-action-row-url-target-scheme-set-closed`, `ui-dashboard-header-action-url-scheme-set-closed` and `ui-action-on-success-navigate-scheme-set-closed`. There is one changeset, `.changeset/23077-url-target-doors-scheme-set.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, BREAKING, with a FROM → TO table and the one-line fix, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and ADR-0087 `registered` with the three ids.

**Empty values.** At the three doors that have no target-required rule (dashboard `actionUrl`, `onSuccess.navigate`, a row's `target`), the predicate judges an empty string like any other value and refuses it. This keeps the predicate's own rule. The runtime does nothing with an empty value either: the dashboard renderer warns on an empty `actionUrl`, `readOnSuccessNavigation` drops an empty `navigate`, and `executeUrl` fails with "No URL provided". The changeset's FROM → TO table names this case.

### The dispatch's mechanism assumptions, as measured

- **A1** (lines). Every door was a free string at `0aef78881`. `dashboard.zod.ts:109` `actionUrl: z.string()` and the three `component.zod.ts` rows at `:3834` / `:3931` / `:4114` matched. `onSuccess.navigate` was at `action.zod.ts:1785`, not `:941`. `:941` is the top-level `navigate` guidance key, a different thing.
- **A2** (red at base). Reproduced through one-time ablations, recorded below. With each door's refinement removed, which is the base behaviour, these pins read red:
  - the schema-level refusals;
  - the `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` / `defineStack` reach pins for the dashboard and `onSuccess` doors;
  - the props-gate pins, where the expected finding is missing because the gate answered 0 findings.
- **A3** (omitted `actionType`). The contract states no default for `actionType`. Its two readers that assign one both assign `'url'`: objectui `DashboardRenderer` builds the header `ActionDef` with `type: (a.actionType) || 'url'`, and this repo's `validateDashboardActionRefs` uses `strName(action.actionType) ?? 'url'`. **Pinned reading: an omitted `actionType` is the url route and is judged.** The renderer's click handler, read at objectui `origin/main` `7af0ab37` and at the pin `7578323`, returns early with a console warning on an omitted `actionType`. So a refused target never works on either reading, and nothing that works today is refused. The click handler's split is an Acceptance note below.
- **A4** (deferred `${`). Held: `${result.redirectUrl}` is accepted at `onSuccess.navigate`, and that is pinned.

### File surface beyond the claim's literal list (declared)

- `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`. `build-schemas.ts` refuses a published schema that gains a refinement it cannot project unless the new site is declared in this ledger. Its own prescription is "Declare it by adding…", and it says "⛔ do not delete or weaken" the rule. The ledger gains 21 sites: 17 in 13 existing entries, and 4 new entries (`ui/DashboardHeaderAction`, `ui/DashboardHeader`, `ui/ActionButtonProps`, `ui/ActionIconProps`). The `measured` header totals are updated to match its body (231 schemas / 734 sites), which `scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts` pins. No site is removed.
- The three D3 entry files. `check-adr-0087-registration` needs them: a changeset with a FROM → TO prescription cannot claim `no-migration-prescription`.
- `content/docs/references/ui/{action,dashboard,component}.mdx`, regenerated by `gen:docs`. `check:generated` named only `check:docs`.

## Verification record

That is 22 files. Most of them are notify-node `actionUrl` or React `onSuccess` callbacks, which are different keys.
  - **The static census behind it.** Every `actionUrl:`, `navigate:` and url-adjacent `target:` literal in this repository, tests included, is either admitted or not on a url route. The exceptions are this PR's own pins and three raw-object fixtures in `validate-dashboard-action-refs.test.ts`, which the spec never parses (see the Acceptance notes).

    - src leg: **4 failed / 21 passed**, the four row refusals.

Both exit 0 after a workspace build through the lock, at the same head. `--ran` reconciles: "112 derived, 111 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", and every line carries its exit code. `check:nul-bytes` is green, and a raw control-byte scan of the 13 touched files finds 0 lines.

At e9ff53c82: spec suite 660 files / 20010 passed / 1 todo; lint suite 138 files / 6617 passed / 5 skipped; dispatch-gates --ran 112 derived, 111 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (check:type-check-debt, by order), 0 UNRUN.

## Acceptance notes

- **objectui's dashboard header click handler bypasses the classifier** (read at objectui `7af0ab37`, `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx:1211-1223`). An `actionType: 'url'` header action is navigated by the renderer itself, not through `ActionRunner` / `classifyNavigationTarget`:
  - it calls `location.assign` for `^https?://` **or a `//`-prefixed** target;
  - it calls `history.pushState` for everything else, which throws on `mailto:` and admits a bare `thanks`;
  - an omitted `actionType` is skipped with a warning, while the same file's `headerActionDefs` defaults it to `'url'`.

  This is a second URL grammar on the runtime side of ruling A+. Reported to the seat with evidence in the dev report; it is not fixed here (objectui).
- **A page action row's `onSuccess` is `z.unknown()`**, forwarded to the runner's `navigateOnSuccess`. Measured through the dist: `ActionButtonPropsSchema` and an `action:group` member accept `onSuccess: { navigate: 'javascript:alert(1)' }`, and the props gate answers 0 findings. As a control, `ActionSchema` refuses the same value at `onSuccess.navigate`. This is the same family, but declaring the rows' `onSuccess` shape is a contract choice and not a mechanical fix, so it is reported to the seat and not fixed here.
- `actionType: 'navigation'` on a page action row reaches the runner's `executeNavigation`, an alias of `url`, and its `target` is not judged here. The row's `actionType` is a free string, and no producer writes it. This is a residual of the family; the card and the claim scope the rows to `'url'`.
- Three fixtures in `packages/lint/src/validate-dashboard-action-refs.test.ts` (`//cdn.example.com/y` and `some-handler` with `actionType: 'url'`, and `do_something` with it omitted) feed the gate raw objects. They stay green, but they now pin inputs that the stack parse refuses before the gate sees them.
- `action.form.ts`'s help text for `onSuccess.navigate` still says "A relative value is an in-app route". The `describe` text now states the set.
- The props gate's generic `component-props-invalid` text ("nothing refuses it today, so the renderer receives the props as written") reads loosely for these rows, because the runner does refuse at the click.
